memory_update.text: AVGO is a high-confidence direct candidate for AI cluster fabric due to official AI revenue disclosure and Tomahawk/Jericho Ethernet switch ASIC positioning.
ANET is a high-confidence systems/software candidate for Ethernet AI fabrics; later layers should separate durable AI back-end deployments from general cloud refresh and campus/routing growth.
MRVL is a high-confidence connectivity semiconductor candidate across optical DSPs, coherent DSPs, SerDes, and custom silicon; key open question is revenue mix and design-win durability.
LITE is a direct optics/photonic-component candidate, strengthened by NVIDIA’s 2026 strategic agreement; key risks are customer concentration, capacity execution, and cyclical telecom/datacom mix.
FN is a second-order optical manufacturing/packaging candidate; include because manufacturing yield and precision optical assembly may become hidden bottlenecks behind transceiver OEMs.

Not included due to 5-candidate cap but should be evaluated in later passes: COHR for optical transceivers/lasers/materials and NVIDIA partnership; CIEN for DCI/coherent optics and WaveLogic; CSCO/HPE/JNPR/NOK for networking systems; AAOI for smaller optical-module exposure; CIEN/COHR/LITE/FN comparisons need AI revenue purity checks.

node: AI networking, optics, and cluster fabric
summary: Expanded US-listed universe for the AI cluster-fabric node. The strongest direct exposures are merchant/custom networking silicon, Ethernet switching systems, optical DSP/SerDes/connectivity semiconductors, photonic components/lasers, and precision optical manufacturing. This pass prioritizes suppliers whose products may become capacity or qualification chokepoints as AI clusters move from accelerator scarcity toward fabric, optics, congestion control, and observability constraints. This is research support only, not a trading recommendation.
